vis.scope: Input MS or CalTable (blank for none)

gridrows.scope: Number of subplot rows Averaged visibility ordinate lists retain the requested page capacity.

gridcols.scope: Number of subplot columns Averaged visibility ordinate lists retain the requested page capacity.

rowindex.scope: Choose the zero-based row of a single noniterated MeasurementSet visibility plot.

colindex.scope: Choose the zero-based column of a single noniterated MeasurementSet visibility plot. A Time versus observed amplitude scan sequence can start in the right cell of a one-row two-column grid.

xaxis.scope: Plot x-axis (blank for default/current) Unaveraged visibilities can be plotted against integration interval in seconds or UV, U, V and W in wavelengths. Ordinary vector time averaging weights U, V, W and UV distance coordinates with the selected visibilities and row weights. Unaveraged channel plots can combine three or more visibility and metre baseline or observatory elevation ordinates with separate sample masks. Pair raw Antenna1/2, Observation, Intent and Feed1/2 with a visibility axis. Row uses the selected table's numbers for a single spectral window. Unaveraged Time and Channel can be paired with row or buffer identifiers using their collapsed sample masks. Unaveraged antenna pointing pairs use degree coordinates in the requested direction frame. Channel and Time can be paired with one channel-averaged derived visibility ordinate. Time can be paired with one ordinary vector-time-averaged observed or corrected model expression.

xdatacolumn.scope: Use a stored MeasurementSet visibility column or an unaveraged vector or scalar residual or model ratio for X independently of Y. Unaveraged real and signed amplitude axes can use FLOAT_DATA. A blank selector uses observed data for a new plot. Selected virtual models supply unaveraged, channel-only and ordinary vector or scalar time-averaged model coordinates without materializing a MODEL_DATA column. Complex inputs without a stored or applicable virtual model use the default visibility model. Additional column forms remain open. Channel and ordinary vector time averaging support separately weighted stored visibility columns. In a single-ordinate channel-only plot, vector and scalar corrected-minus-model and corrected-over-model use the separately averaged stored operands and a separately weighted observed or corrected visibility axis. Channel-only observed DATA/model expressions use the observed spectrum for DATA and the calibrated spectrum for MODEL_DATA when CORRECTED_DATA exists. With no corrected column, the model uses the observed spectrum and the corrected expression falls back to DATA. Ordinary vector time averaging pairs separately weighted observed, corrected or model coordinates and vector or scalar model expressions on the two visibility axes. With both time and channel averaging, independent visibility axes can also pair stored or derived observed, corrected and model coordinates. Ordinary scalar time averaging also supports stored observed and corrected residuals and ratios paired with Time, Channel, or an independently selected visibility coordinate. Supported channel-only and ordinary time-averaged model expressions use the selected virtual or default model when applicable.

xframe.scope: Set a scalar control on the X antenna direction axis. Choose ICRS, J2000, B1950, Galactic or geodetic azimuth/elevation.

xinterp.scope: Set a scalar control on the X antenna direction axis. Choose nearest segment-start sampling or natural cubic spline interpolation.

yaxis.scope: Plot a single ordinate or a list. Unaveraged and channel-only averaged MeasurementSet visibility lists can contain more than two independent ordinates. Unaveraged visibilities can be plotted against integration interval in seconds or UV, U, V and W in wavelengths. Channel-only averages project transformed weight and sigma rows and spectra against stored visibility coordinates. Ordinary vector time averaging weights U, V, W and UV distance coordinates with the selected visibilities and row weights. Unaveraged channel plots can combine three or more visibility and metre baseline or observatory elevation ordinates with separate sample masks. Pair raw Antenna1/2, Observation, Intent and Feed1/2 with a visibility axis. Row uses the selected table's numbers for a single spectral window. Unaveraged Time and Channel can be paired with row or buffer identifiers using their collapsed sample masks. Unaveraged antenna pointing pairs use degree coordinates in the requested direction frame. Independent stored visibility ordinate lists also support ordinary vector and scalar time averages.

ydatacolumn.scope: Use a stored MeasurementSet visibility column or an unaveraged vector or scalar residual or model ratio for Y independently of X. Unaveraged real and signed amplitude axes can use FLOAT_DATA. Unaveraged and channel-only averaged visibility ordinates can choose independent stored columns, including ordinates of the same axis type. Missing column list entries use observed data. Selected virtual models supply unaveraged, channel-only and ordinary vector or scalar time-averaged model coordinates without materializing a MODEL_DATA column. Complex inputs without a stored or applicable virtual model use the default visibility model. Additional column forms and other mixed visibility and metadata ordinate lists remain open. Channel and ordinary vector time averaging support separately weighted stored visibility columns. In a single-ordinate channel-only plot, vector and scalar corrected-minus-model and corrected-over-model use the separately averaged stored operands and a separately weighted observed or corrected visibility axis. Channel-only observed DATA/model expressions use the observed spectrum for DATA and the calibrated spectrum for MODEL_DATA when CORRECTED_DATA exists. With no corrected column, the model uses the observed spectrum and the corrected expression falls back to DATA. A single stored corrected/model or observed/model expression can be plotted after channel averaging against Channel or Time. With Time as X, ordinary vector time averaging projects one observed or corrected residual or ratio after separately averaging the stored visibility and model operands. Float scalar projections retain signed amplitude differences and the full phase difference. Ordinary vector time averaging pairs separately weighted observed, corrected or model coordinates and vector or scalar model expressions on the two visibility axes. With both time and channel averaging, independent visibility axes can also pair stored or derived observed, corrected and model coordinates. With scalar=True, Time can be paired with one stored corrected residual formed by subtracting the separately averaged amplitudes and phases. Ordinary scalar time averaging also supports stored observed and corrected residuals and ratios paired with Time, Channel, or an independently selected visibility coordinate. Supported channel-only and ordinary time-averaged model expressions use the selected virtual or default model when applicable.

yframe.scope: Set a scalar control on the Y antenna direction axis. Choose ICRS, J2000, B1950, Galactic or geodetic azimuth/elevation.

yinterp.scope: Set a scalar control on the Y antenna direction axis. Choose nearest segment-start sampling or natural cubic spline interpolation.

yaxislocation.scope: Choose the left or right side. PlotMS groups more than two unaveraged or channel-only averaged MeasurementSet visibility ordinates by side. An omitted position defaults to left. A scalar location does not apply to an ordinate list. Unaveraged iterated MeasurementSet panels group their visibility ordinates by side.

avgchannel.scope: Average selected channels into bins. MeasurementSet data, corrected and model axes use the corresponding spectral weights when available, including lists of independent ordinates. Channel averaging composes with ordinary vector time averaging. Vector baseline averaging can follow channel averaging at each integration. Vector time and channel averages can both precede the baseline reducer. Channel-only averages project transformed weight and sigma rows and spectra against stored visibility coordinates. A selected fully masked combined vector average exports an empty product. Channel-only corrected vector and scalar residuals and ratios project their stored complex operands after averaging with calibrated weights. Observed and model operands can use independent selected spectra before vector or scalar projection. A lone derived visibility ordinate uses the same separate stored operand spectra and observed-cube mask with a Channel or Time abscissa. Time and channel averaging can compose before projecting a stored observed or corrected vector or scalar residual or ratio against Channel or Time, with the selected cube mask and separate operand sums. Observed spectra follow the weight-to-sigma conversion between stages. With both time and channel averaging, independent visibility axes can also pair stored or derived observed, corrected and model coordinates. Supported derived plots with channel and scalar time averaging reduce complex channels before reducing amplitude and phase in time. Stored visibility plots can use complex channel averaging followed by scalar time averaging with independent columns and two stored ordinates. Complex channels can be averaged before per-antenna reduction. The per-antenna stage uses the transformed spectral weight and retains the output antenna identity and order. Vector time and complex channel averages compose before antenna reduction, using the transformed weight spectrum to reduce by antenna. Ordinary stored visibility plots can use vector time and channel transforms with independent spectra, equal stored-model channel means and cube-flag masks. Supported channel and channel/time residuals and ratios use selected virtual or default model operands. Channel-averaged visibility ordinate lists can produce static correlation, scan and field panels. Channel and time averages of independent stored ordinate lists can also span scans and fields. Supported channel and baseline averaging accepts lists of independent stored visibility ordinates. Supported per-antenna channel and time averaging accepts lists of independent stored visibility ordinates. Channel bins compose with independent stored visibility ordinate lists in spectral-window averages.

avgtime.scope: Average selected samples over the requested interval in seconds. Ordinary MeasurementSet vector time averaging can use two independent stored ordinate columns with a visibility, time, channel or frequency abscissa. Channel and time averaging can be combined for those axes. The baseline reducer can combine the visibility iterator’s vector time averages. Vector time and channel averages can both precede the baseline reducer. The ordinary scalar mode uses PlotMS visibility-buffer boundaries. Ordinary vector time averaging weights U, V, W and UV distance coordinates with the selected visibilities and row weights. A selected fully masked combined vector average exports an empty product. Ordinary vector time averaging can pair Time with one stored observed or corrected vector or scalar residual or ratio, using separate operand weights and the selected cube mask before projection. Ordinary vector time averaging pairs separately weighted observed, corrected or model coordinates and vector or scalar model expressions on the two visibility axes. Time and channel averaging can compose before projecting a stored observed or corrected vector or scalar residual or ratio against Channel or Time, with the selected cube mask and separate operand sums. Observed spectra follow the weight-to-sigma conversion between stages. With both time and channel averaging, independent visibility axes can also pair stored or derived observed, corrected and model coordinates. With scalar=True, Time can be paired with one stored corrected residual formed by subtracting the separately averaged amplitudes and phases. Ordinary scalar time averaging also supports stored observed and corrected residuals and ratios paired with Time, Channel, or an independently selected visibility coordinate. Supported derived plots with channel and scalar time averaging reduce complex channels before reducing amplitude and phase in time. Stored visibility plots can use complex channel averaging followed by scalar time averaging with independent columns and two stored ordinates. Scalar per-antenna averages can use closed time intervals with their original buffer interval centers, including after complex channel averaging. Ordinary vector time averages can feed per-antenna reduction using the transformed weight spectrum and closed second-stage time intervals. Vector time and complex channel averages compose before antenna reduction, using the transformed weight spectrum to reduce by antenna. Ordinary stored visibility plots can use vector time and channel transforms with independent spectra, equal stored-model channel means and cube-flag masks. Ordinary vector and scalar time averaging also accepts lists of three or more independent stored visibility ordinates, with optional complex channel bins. Selected virtual models can be predicted before ordinary vector and scalar time averages, including optional channel bins and independent observed or corrected axes. Supported vector and scalar time residuals and ratios also use selected virtual or default model operands. Supported ordinary time-averaged visibility ordinate lists can produce static correlation, scan and field panels. Supported vector and scalar time averages of stored visibility ordinate lists can span scans and fields. Supported baseline and time averaging can retain three or more independent stored ordinate columns. Supported antenna and time averages accept independent stored visibility ordinate lists. Time and spectral-window averaging can compose with independent stored visibility ordinate lists and scan and field spans.

avgscan.scope: Permit time bins to cross scan boundaries. For two independent MeasurementSet visibility ordinates, vector averaging keeps the requested grouping and uses the first chronological integration for the bin metadata. Scan and field spans also apply to supported vector time-averaged derived expressions and their composition with channel averaging. Ordinary scalar time averaging also spans scans and fields, retaining the first field and reporting scan -1 when a bin combines scans. Channel averaging followed by scalar time averaging also spans scans and fields, retaining the first field and reporting scan -1 when a bin combines scans. Scalar and vector per-antenna time averaging can span scans, fields or both. Each unselected span retains its barrier and exports use the averaged buffer identifiers. Supported vector time residuals can use a selected virtual model when spanning scans. Three or more independent stored visibility ordinates can share a scan-spanning vector or scalar time average. Supported spanned time and spectral-window averages accept independent stored visibility ordinate lists.

avgfield.scope: Permit time bins to cross field boundaries. For two independent MeasurementSet visibility ordinates, vector averaging keeps the requested grouping and uses the first chronological integration for the bin metadata. Scan and field spans also apply to supported vector time-averaged derived expressions and their composition with channel averaging. Ordinary scalar time averaging also spans scans and fields, retaining the first field and reporting scan -1 when a bin combines scans. Channel averaging followed by scalar time averaging also spans scans and fields, retaining the first field and reporting scan -1 when a bin combines scans. Scalar and vector per-antenna time averaging can span scans, fields or both. Each unselected span retains its barrier and exports use the averaged buffer identifiers. Three or more independent stored visibility ordinates can share a field-spanning vector or scalar time average. Supported spanned time and spectral-window averages accept independent stored visibility ordinate lists.

avgbaseline.scope: Vector-average selected baselines within each integration for stored MeasurementSet visibility axes. Use the scalar weight of the first selected correlation for all plotted visibility columns. Vector baseline averaging can follow channel averaging at each integration. The baseline reducer can combine the visibility iterator’s vector time averages. Vector time and channel averages can both precede the baseline reducer. Scalar baseline averages accumulate weighted amplitudes and phases. They also compose with a preceding complex channel average and scalar time bins, including supported independent visibility and stored residual coordinates. Supported scalar residuals can also use selected virtual or default model operands. Vector and scalar baseline averaging accept three or more independent stored visibility ordinates.

avgantenna.scope: Average per antenna (mutually exclusive with avgbaseline) Static per-antenna visibility exports at individual integrations use the averaged antenna ID and name and follow integration, antenna, channel and correlation order. Scalar antenna averages use independently averaged amplitude and phase with a common visibility weight. They include the conjugated contribution from each second endpoint. Extended antenna averages remain partial. Complex channels can be averaged before per-antenna reduction. The per-antenna stage uses the transformed spectral weight and retains the output antenna identity and order. Scalar per-antenna averages can use closed time intervals with their original buffer interval centers, including after complex channel averaging. Ordinary vector time averages can feed per-antenna reduction using the transformed weight spectrum and closed second-stage time intervals. Vector time and complex channel averages compose before antenna reduction, using the transformed weight spectrum to reduce by antenna. Scalar and vector per-antenna time averaging can span scans, fields or both. Each unselected span retains its barrier and exports use the averaged buffer identifiers. Vector and scalar per-antenna averaging accept three or more independent stored visibility ordinates.

avgspw.scope: Average the selected spectral windows. Ordinary stored visibility plots support scalar and vector reduction with an optional preceding channel average. Each window contributes its selected channels by position. Displayed channel and frequency coordinates come from the first input window, including for baselines first seen in a later window. Scalar time and SPW averaging uses closed intervals, including with scan and field spans and a preceding complex channel average. Such a bin keeps the first SPW ID and displays the spectral coordinates of the last attached input buffer. Ordinary vector time and SPW averages first reduce each baseline and window with the selected visibility spectra, then form closed PlotMS groups from the returned buffers. Vector time and SPW averages can also use complex channel bins after the visibility time transform and span scans or fields independently. Vector and scalar spectral-window averaging accepts independent stored visibility ordinate lists.

scalar.scope: Scalar averaging (False=vector averaging) Ordinary MeasurementSet channel-only averaging uses vector visibilities, and the text header retains the requested scalar control. Ordinary scalar time averaging uses the first selected correlation’s row weight and reduces amplitude and phase separately for stored visibility axes. With scalar=True, Time can be paired with one stored corrected residual formed by subtracting the separately averaged amplitudes and phases. Ordinary scalar time averaging also supports stored observed and corrected residuals and ratios paired with Time, Channel, or an independently selected visibility coordinate. Ordinary scalar time averaging also spans scans and fields, retaining the first field and reporting scan -1 when a bin combines scans. Supported derived plots with channel and scalar time averaging reduce complex channels before reducing amplitude and phase in time. Stored visibility plots can use complex channel averaging followed by scalar time averaging with independent columns and two stored ordinates. Channel averaging followed by scalar time averaging also spans scans and fields, retaining the first field and reporting scan -1 when a bin combines scans. Scalar baseline averages accumulate weighted amplitudes and phases. They also compose with a preceding complex channel average and scalar time bins, including supported independent visibility and stored residual coordinates. Standalone per-antenna scalar averages use the same amplitude and phase components, including Real and Imag projections. Scalar per-antenna averages can use closed time intervals with their original buffer interval centers, including after complex channel averaging. Supported scalar time or baseline residuals and ratios can use selected virtual or default model operands. Ordinary scalar time-averaged visibility ordinate lists can use supported static correlation, scan and field iteration. Scalar time averaging across scans and fields also supports independent stored visibility ordinate lists. Supported scalar baseline averaging can use lists of independent stored visibility ordinates with time and channel bins. Supported scalar per-antenna averaging can use three or more independent stored ordinate columns. Scalar spectral-window averaging accepts independent stored visibility ordinate lists.

behaviors.title: Read MeasurementSets and calibration tables
behaviors.scope: Open casacore MeasurementSets and current, BPOLY and GSPLINE calibration tables through vis or caltable, preserving the public None return and input-path checks.
behaviors.gap: Remaining MeasurementSet plotting paths are open under #1032 and #215.

behaviors.title: Select solution samples
behaviors.scope: Select solution rows and channels by field, window, time, antenna, scan, observation, polarization, antenna-position component and TaQL. Refuse unsupported modern calibration selectors. Resolve GSPLINE selection directly against source table rows and CAL_DESC. Route ordinary MeasurementSet visibility plots through native row, baseline, channel, correlation and flag selection. Apply the same feed predicate to the selected visibility rows and the row selection used by atmospheric overlays.
behaviors.gap: Remaining MeasurementSet selection paths are open under #1032 and #215.

behaviors.title: Project axes and flags
behaviors.scope: Read complex and real parameter cells and select calibration axes. Keep flagged sample visibility consistent in text and image products. Validate active axis and range controls before writing. Use the reference axes for Tsys and antenna-position products. Evaluate stored BPOLY and GSPLINE coefficients and expose their solution flags and metadata. Plot independent stored MeasurementSet DATA, CORRECTED_DATA and MODEL_DATA axes and unaveraged vector and scalar residuals or model ratios with the shared sample mask. Use DATA for corrected axes, residuals and ratios when the stored corrected column is absent on a complex MeasurementSet. Use FLOAT_DATA for observed visibilities on unaveraged mixed inputs and signed amplitude or real axes on float-only inputs. Keep the requested order and column identity for independent unaveraged visibility ordinates and group them by figure side. Use the default visibility model for complex data without a stored model or an applicable virtual recipe. Predict selected virtual component and Fourier models through the native visibility model engine. Plot unaveraged visibility axes with integration interval and UVW in wavelengths using the selected visibility buffer and per-channel frequency. Unaveraged channel plots of three or more axes on Y use separate masks for visibility, U, V, W and observatory elevation ordinates. Plot raw row and buffer identifiers with selected visibility axes and use distinct STATE observing mode IDs for Intent. Use each metadata-only Time or Channel pair's dimensions to collapse selected visibility flags and report its compact point identifiers. Pair Time, antenna longitude and antenna latitude with selected cube masks, nearest or spline interpolation, and independently chosen scalar direction frames.
behaviors.gap: Averaged pointing, list-valued pointing controls, sample masks for other mixed visibility and metadata axes, additional averaging modes and additional MS column forms are open. Averaged interval and wavelength coordinates and reporting-frame transforms for these axes remain open.

behaviors.title: Average selected plot samples
behaviors.scope: Average calibration solutions in weighted channel and time bins with scan, field, antenna, baseline and spectral-window controls. Keep flagged channel frequency coordinates consistent with the CASA cache. For MeasurementSets, independently channel-average stored visibility columns while applying each column's spectral weights and the selected channel flags. Ordinary vector time averaging uses the selected integrations, per-column weights and the MeasurementSet transform time groups. Channel averaging can follow ordinary vector time averaging. The primary channel weights determine which averaged bins render. Vector time bins can span the requested scan and field boundaries. Vector baseline averages use the visibility iterator order and preserve separate observations. Text exports use synthetic antenna IDs. For combined channel and baseline averages, each visibility column is averaged across channels before the baseline reducer applies the transformed scalar weight. Combined vector time and baseline averages follow the subchunks emitted by the time-averaging iterator and use their interval bounds. With all three vector controls, baseline weights come from the time-accumulated and channel-binned spectra. Ordinary scalar time averaging uses the raw visibility buffer windows and separate amplitude and phase means. Channel-averaged statistical coordinates use transformed spectra, the selected cube mask and the observed or calibrated column role. Baseline coordinates for ordinary vector time averaging use the transform row weights and the selected cube mask.
behaviors.gap: Scalar combinations with other averaging controls, antenna and spectral-window averaging, fully masked exports, effective FLOAT_DATA and derived visibility averages, and additional flagged and weight coordinates remain under #1032.

behaviors.title: Lay out and export plot pages
behaviors.scope: Partition selected series across a grid. Text uses the requested grid capacity. Image export provides current and all-page ranges and names the physical outputs in successful completions. A noniterated MeasurementSet visibility plot occupies the requested grid cell. Offset MeasurementSet scan pages account for the starting cell when exporting images.
behaviors.gap: Other offset iteration combinations, calibration-table placement, persistent pages and additional presentation modes remain open.

behaviors.title: Render the shared plot document
behaviors.scope: Transfer native arrays through the existing binary payload and draw them in the shared Matplotlib renderer. Apply plot titles, labels, marker size and shape, connectors, grids, legend, page headers and export sizing. Show or hide the clear and flagged symbols independently for unaveraged MeasurementSet visibility pairs.
behaviors.gap: Renderer-specific marker fill patterns and interactive editing remain open.

behaviors.title: Save and publish selected plot products
behaviors.scope: Write current and legacy calibration coordinates and metadata as text and render figures through the shared Python presenter. Publish requested files and preserve existing files when overwrite is false. Export ordinary MeasurementSet visibility coordinates and independent stored visibility columns as text and figures. Export calibrated MeasurementSet text and paginated figures, including atmospheric curves. Write a successful empty text section and figure for fully hidden raw visibility pairs.
behaviors.gap: More export, multi-plot state and interactive display forms remain open.

behaviors.title: Advanced calibration plotting controls
behaviors.scope: Apply calibration libraries to MeasurementSet plots in memory. Compute transmission, sky temperature and receiver sidebands for MeasurementSets and calibration tables, including selected channels and requested overlay color groups.
behaviors.gap: Remaining shared PlotMS forms are tracked in #1032 and #215.

decisions.inputs: A PlotMS request with selectdata=False and supplied selection text.
decisions.casa: Raises Exception with message updateImmediately must be a boolean.
decisions.ours: Displays and exports all available solution points without applying the selector text.
decisions.rationale: Make the documented selection switch work when it is false.
decisions.impact: The native request produces all 160 available points in the paired fixture. The same fallback preserves all 1,920 points in the unfiltered callibrary case.
decisions.record: PlotMS disabling selection calls the selection setter with a missing argument

decisions.inputs: Modern calibration input with an unsupported selector, invalid antenna-position selector or empty TaQL selection.
decisions.casa: Refuses the plot with an RPC failure whose details say plot parameters failed.
decisions.ours: Refuses the plot with a task parameter error describing the selector or empty row set.
decisions.rationale: Give the caller the cause using the native task error contract.
decisions.impact: Both workflows preserve an absent export on selection failure.

decisions.inputs: A five-antenna GSPLINE table plotted with antenna="!A2".
decisions.casa: Displays only antenna A2, despite negation.
decisions.ours: Displays A0, A1, A3 and A4.
decisions.rationale: Honor the documented antenna exclusion instead of passing the excluded ID to the plot cache.
decisions.impact: The displayed antenna membership follows the source-row filter.
decisions.record: PlotMS shows the excluded antenna on a GSPLINE plot
